output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: StringUtils.quoteAndEscape() (the 6-arg escapePattern overload, reached from Shell.getRawCommandLine via Commandline.getShellCommandline/execute) short-circuited and returned `source` unchanged whenever it started and ended with the quote delimiter, skipping all neutralization. Attacker-controlled arguments beginning and ending with a single quote but containing interior quotes/metacharacters therefore passed through to /bin/sh -c verbatim.

Fix: replaced the unconditional pre-quoted shortcut with a guarded one. It still trusts an already-wrapped token, but for the single-quote delimiter it additionally requires that the delimiter appears only as the outer wrapper (source.indexOf('\'',1) == length-1). Malicious args with interior single quotes now fall through to escape()+wrap, producing '\''-style escaping that keeps the injected text as a literal argument. For non-single-quote delimiters the original behaviour is preserved, so BourneShell executable paths pre-quoted by unifyQuotes (which escapes interior double quotes as \") are not doubly quoted.

Considered but rejected: fully removing the shortcut (the exploiter's simulated patch). It neutralizes the POV but double-quotes the executable (unifyQuotes already wraps it), producing ""..."" and breaking testQuotedPathWithQuotationMark / testQuotedPathWithQuotationMarkAndApostrophe / testGetShellCommandLineBash_WithSingleQuotedArg. The delimiter-aware guard fixes the vuln while keeping all existing behaviour.

Added regression test testQuote_EscapeBrokenPreQuotedArgument asserting an interior-breakout single-quoted argument is fully escaped rather than returned verbatim.

Verification: POV (bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh) now prints "RESULT: NOT VULNERABLE", exits 1, and creates no /tmp/plexus_pov_injected_marker. `mvn -B test` = 284 tests, 0 failures/0 errors.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only narrows which pre-quoted strings are trusted verbatim; it never loosens escaping. Behaviour for double-quote and other delimiters is unchanged, so executable-path quoting (including exotic paths containing quotes/spaces) is preserved, as confirmed by the full existing suite. The single-quote path now escapes any argument whose interior contains a single quote — a strict superset of neutralization vs. before, with no legitimate use case relying on interior-quote pass-through (POSIX single-quoted strings cannot contain single quotes anyway). Note: for the double-quote delimiter the shortcut still trusts pre-quoted tokens verbatim, so `$`/backtick inside a double-quoted executable path are not neutralized here — this is pre-existing behaviour for internally-generated executable paths and outside the scope of this argument-injection finding.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-078 OS command injection in plexus-utils by hardening StringUtils.quoteAndEscape(). The method previously returned any argument verbatim if it merely started and ended with the quote delimiter, so a BourneShell argument like "'a' ; touch <marker> ; 'b'" broke out of the single quotes and injected a command into the string passed to /bin/sh -c. The shortcut is now delimiter-aware: for the single-quote argument delimiter it only trusts a pre-quoted token when the delimiter never appears in the interior (a POSIX single-quoted string is fully literal and cannot contain even an escaped single quote), so any interior single quote forces full escaping. Other delimiters (e.g. the double-quote executable delimiter, whose interior quotes are backslash-escaped by BourneShell.unifyQuotes) keep the original behaviour, avoiding double-quoting of executable paths. The POV now exits 1 and creates no marker; the full test suite (284 tests) passes.
